docs / watch

cwm watch

Install or remove a shell hook that records each command with its folder.

$ cwm watch <start|stop|status> [-ex a,b]

How it works

  • watch start adds a block to your profile. The block calls cwm watch log after every command. There is no background process.
  • Commands that look like they hold secrets (password, token, secret, api key, Authorization, bearer, private key) are never stored.
  • Commands that start with a space are never stored.
  • -ex takes a comma separated list of command names to skip, for example cwm,clear. Run watch start -ex ... again to update the list.
  • Read the log back with cwm get -a. Remove duplicates with cwm tidy watch.
  • cwm watch log is internal. The shell hook uses it.

Subcommands

watch start
Install the hook in your shell profile.
watch stop
Remove the hook.
watch status
Show whether the hook is active and the exclusion list.

Flags

-ex, --exclude <list>
Command names to skip, comma separated.
